# sanparks-watch: ground truth for identify_test
#
# One line per ARCHIVED FRAME THAT CONTAINS AN ANIMAL, confirmed by eye by
# Jeremy on 7 September 2026 over the whole of hits/ and frames/.
# Format: <cam>/<YYYYMMDD>/<HHMMSS>   (HHMMSS is UTC, the join key)
#
# Any archived frame NOT listed here was reviewed and contains no animal.
# That is what makes this file a negative set as well as a positive one:
# 524 animal frames against 3,585 reviewed empties out of 4,109 archived.
#
# A frame listed here contains an animal. It does NOT mean the logged blob
# box is on that animal; on the reviewed sample the box lands on the animal
# about 4 times in 16 at night and 2 times in 13 in Kruger daylight.
#
# Jeremy's note, 7 September: a few very small birds or small mammals may
# have been missed in review. Treat the empty set as accurate to within that.
#
# Add a line when a new animal frame is confirmed. Nothing reads the order.

# APPENDED 20 September 2026: 658 Nossob frames confirmed by eye to contain an
# animal, 8 to 18 September 2026, from Jeremy's review of Passes A, B1 and C.
# Every one carries a CSV row in logs/nossob/, and the review's day/night
# column agrees with the log's own `mode` column on all 658.
#
# The remaining 863 keys of the same pass are eye-confirmed EMPTY: they are in
# reviewed.txt and not here. Nossob now carries 1,037 animal frames against 2,205
# confirmed empties, 863 of them in daylight.
#
# WHERE THE BOX LANDS, measured on the same pass and recorded here because this
# file is the place people look for it: 518 of the 658 have the logged blob box
# ON the animal and 140 do not, judged on Jeremy's note per frame with silence
# meaning the box is right. By mode that is 447 of 522 at night and 71 of 136
# in daylight. A key in this file says an animal is present. It still does not
# say the row measures it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
